tldr: This paper studies mode splitting in a pump-enhanced ring cavity due to weak Bragg reflection from a nonlinear crystal, affecting mid-infrared generation efficiency.
motivation: To understand and mitigate the detrimental effect of intra-cavity reflection on the enhancement factor in ring cavities used for frequency conversion.
method: Experimental observation of spectral mode splitting in a ring cavity with a periodically-poled nonlinear crystal, compared with a linear cavity; numerical simulations support the findings.
result: Even a tiny reflection (0.0003) causes significant mode splitting in a ring cavity, reducing the enhancement factor, while a linear cavity is immune to this effect.
conclusion: Linear cavities are preferable for pump-enhanced frequency conversion with periodically-poled crystals to avoid mode splitting and achieve higher enhancement.

title: Controlled Generation Of Ultrafast Vector Vortex Beams From A Mode-locked Fiber Laser
authors: Kun Huang, Jing Zeng, Jiwei Gan, Qiang Hao, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on a new class of mode-locked fiber laser that allows direct creation of ultrafast vector vortex beams at arbitrary positions on the higher-order Poincar\'{e} sphere. The on-demand generation of space-variant polarization patterns was realized by controlling geometric phases inside the laser resonator to map polarization to orbital angular momentum. Thanks to the ingenious cavity design, the required intracavity manipulation of the geometric phase imposed no disturbance on the passively mode-locked operation, thus demonstrating robust and flexible switching of vectorial modes with a 8.5-ps pulse duration. Analytical expressions were deduced to model the generated cylindrically-symmetric polarization profiles, and agreed exceedingly well with experimental observations. The presented fiber laser would constitute a compact light source for producing ultrafast pulses in high-purity structured modes, which may find broad applications in classical and quantum optics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a mode-locked fiber laser that generates ultrafast vector vortex beams with controlled polarization patterns.
motivation: To create a compact, robust source of ultrafast vector vortex beams for applications in classical and quantum optics.
method: By controlling geometric phases inside the laser resonator to map polarization to orbital angular momentum, enabling on-demand generation of space-variant polarization patterns.
result: Achieved 8.5-ps pulse duration with flexible switching of vectorial modes; analytical models matched experimental observations.
conclusion: The fiber laser provides a practical source for high-purity structured modes, with potential applications in optical communication, imaging, and quantum optics.

title: Broadband Chromatic Dispersion Of Thermo-refractive Coefficients And Its Impact In Silicon Nitride Nonlinear Photonics
authors: Shao-Chien Ou, Gregory Moille, Kartik Srinivasan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The thermo-refractive effect is a cornerstone of frequency and phase tuning in photonic integrated circuits. In particular, it enables control of phase-matching for integrated nonlinear processes. Chromatic dispersion of the group and effective refractive indices and modal confinement are standard considerations in design, but material thermo-refractive coefficients (TRCs) are typically taken to be fixed for the guiding and cladding materials. Here, we demonstrate that the assumption of non-dispersive TRCs across an octave of bandwidth between the telecom and visible results in a significant discrepancy between measured and simulated resonance frequencies of an integrated Si3N4/SiO2 microring resonator. We uncover a 7 % variation in Si3N4 and SiO2 material TRCs across this range, finding that the variation of dneff /dT from material TRCs is 1.3 times that from modal confinement. This accurately matches a temperature-dependent Lorentz oscillator model describing their chromatic dispersion. By integrating these dispersive TRCs into a multi-physics finite-element model, we achieve precise correspondence with experimentally measured temperature-dependent resonance frequency shifts across the octave, including in the context of second harmonic generation devices. Our results provide a physical framework and a universal predictive workflow for the design of high-efficiency, multi-wavelength nonlinear optical processes, fundamentally improving the thermal control of integrated photonic devices.
tldr: This paper investigates the chromatic dispersion of thermo-refractive coefficients in silicon nitride photonics and its impact on nonlinear optical processes.
motivation: Thermo-refractive coefficients are typically assumed non-dispersive, but this assumption leads to discrepancies in resonance frequency predictions across a broad bandwidth. The research aims to model and validate the dispersion of TRCs to improve thermal control in integrated photonic devices.
method: The authors use a temperature-dependent Lorentz oscillator model to describe the chromatic dispersion of Si3N4 and SiO2 TRCs, and integrate these into a multi-physics finite-element model to simulate resonance shifts. Experimental measurements on microring resonators and second harmonic generation devices validate the model.
result: A 7% variation in Si3N4 and SiO2 TRCs is observed across the telecom-to-visible octave, and the variation of dneff/dT from material TRCs is 1.3 times that from modal confinement. The dispersive TRC model accurately matches experimental temperature-dependent resonance shifts.
conclusion: The work provides a physical framework and predictive workflow for designing high-efficiency, multi-wavelength nonlinear optical processes, fundamentally improving thermal control of integrated photonic devices.

title: Optical Chirality Of Membrane Metasurfaces With Broken In-plane Symmetry
authors: Ivan Toftul, Brijesh Kumar, Maxim Gorkunov, Yuri Kivshar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study chiroptical properties of single-layer dielectric membrane metasurfaces with broken in-plane symmetry. In sharp contrast to a common belief that chiral optical phenomena require symmetry breaking in the vertical direction, we show that flat single-layer metasurfaces are capable of strong specific chiral effects. Although the single-layer geometry forbids conventional co-polarized circular dichroism, strong resonant conversion circular dichroism appears to be possible in particular wavelength ranges determined by the spectra of photonic eigenmodes. We explore its origin starting with a [MATH] rotation-symmetric and in-plane mirror-symmetric membrane metasurface and applying to it various in-plane perturbations. Simultaneously breaking of the in-plane mirror symmetry and lifting the rotation symmetry unlocks resonantly enhanced circular conversion dichroism. We derive selection rules for this effect and trace its origin to eigenmode interference and intercoupling using chiral coupled-mode theory.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that single-layer dielectric membrane metasurfaces with broken in-plane symmetry can exhibit strong circular conversion dichroism, challenging the conventional need for vertical symmetry breaking.
motivation: To explore whether flat single-layer metasurfaces can achieve chiral optical effects, which are typically believed to require three-dimensional structures.
method: The authors start with a rotation- and mirror-symmetric membrane metasurface, then apply in-plane perturbations to break symmetry. They use chiral coupled-mode theory to derive selection rules and analyze eigenmode interference.
result: Strong resonant conversion circular dichroism is observed in specific wavelength ranges when both in-plane mirror symmetry and rotation symmetry are broken, enabled by eigenmode interference.
conclusion: The findings open new possibilities for ultrathin chiral photonic devices, with implications for sensing and polarization control, though the paper does not discuss applications directly.

title: On Leadership Emergence In Opinion Dynamics On Social Networks
authors: Martina Alutto, Lorenzo Zino, Karl H. Johansson, Angela Fontan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Leadership in social groups emerges dynamically through interaction and opinion exchange. Empirical evidence indicates that individuals expressing strong opinions tend to gain influence, while sustained leadership critically depends on maintaining alignment with the surrounding social context. Motivated by these observations, we introduce a coupled dynamical model describing the simultaneous evolution of opinions and leadership in a networked population. Extending the Friedkin-Johnsen framework, we represent leadership as a time-varying susceptibility to social influence, which evolves according to a game-theoretic mechanism, consistent with social psychology evidence. Within this setting, agents strengthen their leadership by expressing decisive yet socially coherent opinions, whereas misalignment with the collective state results in a loss of influence. We analyze the coupled dynamics and establish sufficient conditions to identify which agents necessarily emerge as leaders and which act as followers in the social network.
tldr: This paper models leadership emergence in social networks using a coupled opinion dynamics and game-theoretic framework, but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how leadership emerges dynamically in social groups through opinion exchange, motivated by empirical evidence that strong opinions and social alignment influence leadership.
method: Extends the Friedkin-Johnsen model by introducing a time-varying susceptibility to social influence that evolves via a game-theoretic mechanism, coupling opinion dynamics with leadership evolution.
result: Establishes sufficient conditions to identify which agents become leaders and which become followers in a social network based on the coupled dynamics.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical framework for leadership emergence in social networks, with potential applications in understanding social influence and group dynamics.

title: Design Of An Efficient Tunable Dual Narrow-band Mems Mid And Far Ir Emitter With Me-NTA For Industrial And Biomedical Applications
authors: Md. Imran Hasmi, Md. Saffat Gohor, Foez Ahmed, Jaker Hossain
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectrally selective infrared (IR) thermal emitters are gaining much attention now-a-days for sensing, spectroscopy and biomedical applications. In this research, two metasurface incorporated IR emitters are proposed and numerically analyzed using finite element method (FEM). First structure comprises a NiCr heater integrated with a NiCr-based metallic nanotube array (Me-NTA) metasurface to produce a single-narrowband emission in the mid-infrared (MIR) region. Furthermore, an Au-based Me-NTA metasurface on a NiCr-Au hybrid heater subsequently produces dual-narrowband emission in the short-and far-infrared (SIR and FIR) spectrums. Function of these emitters can be explained by Joule heating with the help of DC bias and consequently uniform temperature distribution can be observed along the active region. Simulation analysis shows that NiCr-metasurface based emitter produces single narrow-band near perfect emission centered at 4.5 {\mu}m in MIR region at an operating temperature of 700 K with maximum in-band conversion efficiency (CE) of 32.3% and radiated power of 199 mW. On the other hand, Au-metasurface based emitter generates dual-narrowband emission peaking at 2.5 {\mu}m and 10 {\mu}m, correlating to SIR and FIR subsequently, achieving maximum emission of 93% and 85%, respectively. The in-band CE for this emitter attains 10.4% and 4.4% in the first and second bands, associated with radiated powers of 350 mW and 147 mW, accordingly. Furthermore, execution of the emitter at 500 K reveals FIR emission with reduced power consumption. These results substantiate the possibilities of the suggested emitters in various industrial and biomedical applications.
tldr: This paper designs and simulates MEMS-based tunable dual narrow-band IR emitters using metasurfaces for industrial and biomedical applications.
motivation: To develop spectrally selective IR emitters with narrow-band and tunable emission for sensing, spectroscopy, and biomedical applications.
method: Finite element method (FEM) simulations of two metasurface-integrated IR emitters: one with NiCr heater and NiCr-based metallic nanotube array (Me-NTA) for single-band MIR emission, and another with Au-based Me-NTA on NiCr-Au hybrid heater for dual-band SIR and FIR emission.
result: NiCr-metasurface emitter achieves near-perfect emission at 4.5 μm with 32.3% in-band conversion efficiency (CE) and 199 mW radiated power at 700 K. Au-metasurface emitter achieves dual peaks at 2.5 μm (93% emission) and 10 μm (85% emission) with CEs of 10.4% and 4.4% and radiated powers of 350 mW and 147 mW, respectively.
conclusion: The proposed emitters show potential for industrial and biomedical applications, with tunable emission and reduced power consumption at lower temperatures.

title: Inverse Design Of Realizable Metasurface Based Absorbers Using Improved Conditioning And Diversity Enhanced Progressively Growing GANs
authors: Vineetha Joy, Mohammad Abdullah, Pramit Pal, Anshuman Kumar, Amit Sethi, Hema Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metasurfaces enable precise manipulation of electromagnetic waves for applications such as beam steering, sensing, and stealth technology. However, inverse design of metasurfaces with targeted EM responses remains challenging due to the computational expense of iterative full wave simulation driven optimization and the limited conditioning fidelity and diversity of existing generative approaches. To address these challenges, this paper presents a generative inverse design framework for controllable and physically consistent metasurface synthesis under continuous spectral constraints. The proposed approach employs a progressively growing Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty integrated with feature wise linear modulation based conditioning for stable propagation of continuous spectral and fabrication constraints. EM consistency is embedded directly into the generative learning process through a surrogate assisted spectral alignment loss, enabling physics constrained generation during training. Further, a determinantal point process based diversity regularization strategy is incorporated to generate geometrically diverse yet spectrally consistent realizations for the same target response. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through the generation of practically realizable metasurface absorbers exhibiting diverse reflection characteristics in the frequency range of 2 to 18 GHz. EM simulations validate that the generated designs meet the target specifications with high accuracy. The final proposed framework achieved an average mean squared error of 0.0052, diversity score of 0.8730, band alignment accuracy of 0.8533, and a valid EM design generation percentage of 89.57, clearly demonstrating its capability to generate highly accurate, diverse, electromagnetically consistent and fabrication realizable metasurface configurations.
tldr: This paper presents a generative inverse design framework for metasurface absorbers using progressively growing GANs with physics-constrained learning and diversity regularization.
motivation: Inverse design of metasurfaces with targeted electromagnetic responses is computationally expensive and existing generative approaches suffer from limited fidelity and diversity.
method: A progressively growing Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty is combined with feature-wise linear modulation conditioning and a surrogate-assisted spectral alignment loss to enforce EM consistency; determinantal point process regularization ensures geometric diversity.
result: The framework achieves high accuracy (MSE 0.0052), diversity score 0.8730, band alignment accuracy 0.8533, and 89.57% valid EM designs for metasurface absorbers in 2-18 GHz.
conclusion: The approach enables efficient, physically consistent, and diverse generation of realizable metasurface designs, with potential for broader application in electromagnetic device inverse design.

title: Symmetry-adapted Qubit Encoding With Complete Active Space And Bravyi--Kitaev Mapping For Quantum Chemistry On A Quantum Computer
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a symmetry-adapted qubit encoding with complete active space (SAE-CAS) for quantum chemistry on fault-tolerant and near-term quantum processors. Building on exact-symmetry encodings, we extend symmetry-adapted mappings to approximate [MATH]-symmetries corresponding to frozen-core and virtual orbitals, thereby reducing qubit requirements without significant loss of accuracy. We derive the mapping from the second-quantised Hamiltonian to active-space qubit Hamiltonians, prove its equivalence to the canonical CAS Hamiltonian with frozen-core and virtual-orbital projection, and integrate it with point-group and spin-parity symmetry encodings via affine Clifford transformations to maximise qubit reduction while preserving the target symmetry sector. The same framework also accommodates the Bravyi--Kitaev mapping, yielding an SAE-CAS-BK variant that is unitarily equivalent to SAE-CAS. Numerical benchmarking on nine small molecules using UCCSD and a hardware-efficient shifted-circular-alternating (HE-SCA) ansatz shows that SAE-CAS reduces qubit counts and Pauli-operator weight, yields shallower circuits with fewer parameters, and often accelerates VQE convergence; with HE-SCA it consistently reaches CAS reference energies in cases where JW-CAS does not converge within the tested budgets. We provide an open-source implementation in the Python package QuantumSymmetry. SAE-CAS offers a route to resource-efficient molecular simulations on fault-tolerant and near-term quantum processors.
tldr: This paper presents a symmetry-adapted qubit encoding method for quantum chemistry on quantum computers, reducing qubit counts and circuit depth.
motivation: To reduce the resource requirements (qubits, gates) for quantum chemistry simulations on near-term and fault-tolerant quantum computers.
method: Extends symmetry-adapted encodings to approximate symmetries (frozen-core/virtual orbitals) and integrates with point-group and spin-parity symmetries via affine Clifford transformations; also applies Bravyi-Kitaev mapping.
result: SAE-CAS reduces qubit counts and Pauli weight, yields shallower circuits, and accelerates VQE convergence on nine small molecules.
conclusion: The method offers a resource-efficient route for molecular simulations on quantum processors, with open-source implementation provided.

title: Single-Frequency Symmetry-Empowered Through-Barrier Sensing In Reconfigurable Complex Media
authors: Shuai S. A. Yuan, Viktar Asadchy, Philipp Del Hougne
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mirror symmetry can strongly enhance the transmission of waves through a barrier inside a complex medium. We recently showed that this phenomenon enables quantitative through-barrier sensing: by tuning programmable scatterers on one side of the barrier to maximize the broadband total transmission through the barrier, the characteristics of scatterers at mirror-symmetric positions on the other side of the barrier can be determined. Considering a sufficiently large bandwidth was crucial to ensure that no accidental narrowband asymmetric resonance can outperform the symmetry-induced transmission enhancement. Here, we overcome this scheme's vexing need for a large bandwidth by replacing the underlying frequency diversity with configurational diversity. Specifically, we introduce auxiliary tunable scatterers at mirror-symmetric positions on either side of the barrier and sweep their characteristics through a series of random mirror-symmetric configurations. We tune the programmable main scatterers on one side of the barrier to maximize the average of the total through-barrier transmission over a series of configurations of the auxiliary scatterers at a single frequency, in order to sense the characteristics of the main scatterers on the other side of the barrier. We systematically study the accuracy of our single-frequency sensing scheme based on a multiport-network system model that cascades two mirror-related wave-chaotic cavities with a weakly transmitting barrier in between. We further examine an extension to non-reciprocal chaotic cavities involving circulators. Altogether, our results establish configurational diversity as a route to single-frequency, symmetry-empowered through-barrier sensing in reconfigurable complex media.
tldr: This paper demonstrates single-frequency through-barrier sensing in complex media using configurational diversity instead of broadband frequency diversity.
motivation: Previous symmetry-empowered through-barrier sensing required large bandwidth to avoid accidental asymmetric resonances; the authors aimed to eliminate this bandwidth requirement.
method: They introduced auxiliary tunable scatterers at mirror-symmetric positions on both sides of the barrier and swept their characteristics through random mirror-symmetric configurations, then tuned main scatterers to maximize average transmission at a single frequency.
result: Configurational diversity enables accurate single-frequency sensing, and the scheme extends to non-reciprocal chaotic cavities with circulators.
conclusion: Configurational diversity provides a route to single-frequency, symmetry-empowered through-barrier sensing in reconfigurable complex media, potentially simplifying experimental implementations.

title: Pseudosymmetry, Ricci Soliton And Curvature Inheritance Symmetries Of Friedmann Lema\^itre Robertson Walker Spacetime
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Friedmann--Lema\^{i}tre--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) spacetime, which was first proposed by Friedmann (1922--1924) and Lema\^{i}tre (1927) and subsequently developed by Robertson and Walker (1935), is an isotropic and homogeneous cosmological model of the universe. This paper addresses a significant gap in the differential geometry literature by providing a comprehensive examination of the curvature properties of the FLRW spacetime. It is demonstrated that the FLRW spacetime satisfies the curvature condition R \cdot R - Q(S, R)=L_C Q(g, C) alongside several pseudosymmetric-type conditions related to the conformal and conharmonic curvature tensors. Furthermore, the Tachibana tensors Q(g,C) and Q(S, C) are found to exhibit a linear dependence on the tensor [MATH]. Additionally, the spacetime is shown to be a 2-quasi-Einstein manifold, generalized Roter type and Ein(3). The Ricci tensor is shown to be neither cyclic parallel nor of Codazzi type, yet it satisfies several compatibility requirements concerning the R, C, P, K and W curvature tensors. A thorough analysis of Ricci solitons and curvature inheritance properties reveals that the spacetime admits almost Ricci soliton and [MATH]-Ricci Yamabe soliton structures with respect to the non-Killing soliton vector fields [MATH] and [MATH]. Moreover, the spacetime admits generalized curvature inheritance symmetry properties for the Riemann curvature tensor, as well as for the Weyl conformal, concircular, and conharmonic curvature tensors with respect to the coordinate vector field [MATH] and the gradient of [MATH]. Later, a comparison of the FLRW and Lema\^{i}tre--Tolman--Bondi (LTB) spacetimes is provided in terms of various curvature-related geometric properties and physical characteristics. Finally, a noteworthy conclusion of the entire study is presented.
tldr: This paper studies curvature properties, pseudosymmetry, and Ricci solitons of FLRW spacetime, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To fill a gap in differential geometry literature by comprehensively examining curvature properties of FLRW spacetime.
method: Mathematical analysis using tensor calculus and curvature conditions.
result: FLRW spacetime satisfies various pseudosymmetric-type conditions, is a 2-quasi-Einstein manifold, and admits almost Ricci soliton and Ricci-Yamabe soliton structures.
conclusion: The study provides geometric insights into FLRW spacetime and compares it with LTB spacetime, but has no implications for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Entropy-Compatible Barrier Schemes For Diffusive Fene Flows
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: FENE-type conformation-tensor models impose a finite-extensibility constraint that is absent from Oldroyd--B flow: the conformation tensor must satisfy [MATH] and [MATH]. Positive definiteness alone is therefore insufficient, since a numerical state can remain positive while crossing the singular trace barrier. Even a trace-preserving logarithmic parametrization is not enough by itself: high-order reconstruction can remain inside the finite-extensibility domain while injecting artificial FENE entropy. We develop and analyze a barrier-preserving entropy-compatible discretization for FENE-P type flows with polymer center-of-mass molecular diffusion and for trace-singular FENE-family closures with the same entropy structure. The method combines a trace-barrier free energy, a finite-extensibility logarithmic parametrization, a least-damping entropy-compatible barrier-log reconstruction, molecular diffusion paired with the barrier entropy variable, compatible quadrature for polymeric work, and a scaled FENE stress variable for the small-Weissenberg limit. For admissible discrete states we prove finite-extensibility preservation at entropy quadrature points, existence and bisection computability of the maximal entropy-admissible reconstruction parameter, a fully discrete free-energy inequality with relaxation and molecular-diffusion barrier dissipation, a quantitative AP stress closure, and a fixed-discretization Newtonian limit. A conditional relative-entropy estimate is derived on compact subsets of the finite-extensibility domain. Numerical diagnostics verify barrier preservation, entropy-compatible reconstruction, energy decay, AP closure, coupled velocity--pressure--stress accuracy, and high-Weissenberg robustness near the trace constraint.
tldr: This paper develops entropy-compatible numerical schemes for FENE-type polymer flow models, focusing on preserving finite-extensibility constraints and thermodynamic consistency.
motivation: Standard numerical methods for FENE-type flows can violate the finite-extensibility constraint, leading to unphysical states. The research aims to design discretizations that inherently preserve the trace barrier and entropy structure.
method: The authors combine a trace-barrier free energy, logarithmic parametrization, entropy-compatible reconstruction, molecular diffusion paired with barrier entropy variables, compatible quadrature, and a scaled stress variable for the small-Weissenberg limit.
result: They prove finite-extensibility preservation, existence of maximal entropy-admissible reconstruction, a fully discrete free-energy inequality, quantitative AP stress closure, and Newtonian limit. Numerical tests confirm barrier preservation, energy decay, and high-Weissenberg robustness.
conclusion: The proposed schemes provide a rigorous framework for simulating FENE-type flows with guaranteed physical fidelity, with potential extensions to more complex viscoelastic models.

title: Umbral Methods, Function Factorisation And Generalisation Of The Fourier Transform Method
authors: Giuseppe Dattoli, Roberto Ricci, Tommaso Severati
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a systematic way to construct trigonometric-like functions beyond the classical sine--cosine pair by factorising rational umbral operators. The guiding idea is simple: the usual trigonometric functions may be viewed as cyclic components arising from a finite factorisation, and the same principle can be extended to an [MATH]-fold decomposition of rational umbral expressions. For each integer [MATH], the construction produces [MATH] functions which play the role of higher-order trigonometric components: their sum reconstructs the corresponding umbral function, while the individual components isolate the different cyclic sectors of its expansion. The construction is developed first in the formal umbral setting. The quadratic case [MATH] gives the Gaussian trigonometric functions, in which the cosine-like component is a Gaussian and the sine-like component is its natural umbral companion. The cubic case [MATH] yields a three-component cyclic system and shows how the same idea extends beyond the usual even--odd decomposition. These examples suggest that trigonometric factorisation is not restricted to ordinary rotations, but belongs to a broader cyclic principle in umbral calculus. We then reinterpret the same formal identities through the recently developed analytic umbral framework. In this second step, the cyclic components are realised by Mellin--Barnes pairings, and the root-of-unity decomposition is related to the splitting of the corresponding spectral kernel. This analytic formulation provides contour representations, local expansions, and sectorial asymptotics for the functions obtained formally. Finally, we indicate how the same cyclic kernels act on Fourier transforms. The resulting framework presents higher-order umbral trigonometric functions as natural cyclic components of factorised rational or exponential umbral operators.
tldr: This paper develops a systematic method to construct higher-order trigonometric-like functions via factorisation of umbral operators, extending classical sine-cosine pairs to arbitrary cyclic decompositions.
motivation: To generalise the concept of trigonometric functions beyond the standard even-odd decomposition using umbral calculus, and to provide an analytic framework via Mellin-Barnes representations.
method: The authors factorise rational umbral operators into M cyclic components, constructing M functions that sum to the original umbral function. They then reinterpret these formal identities using analytic umbral methods, employing Mellin-Barnes integrals and root-of-unity decompositions.
result: They obtain explicit constructions for quadratic (Gaussian trigonometric functions) and cubic cases, showing that trigonometric factorisation follows a cyclic principle. The analytic formulation yields contour representations, local expansions, and sectorial asymptotics.
conclusion: The work establishes a broader cyclic principle in umbral calculus, with potential applications to Fourier transforms and special functions, but does not directly connect to the user's research interests in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Analytic Umbral Transmutations And Bessel Moments
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an analytic umbral approach to Bessel moments, using them as a concrete testbed justifying the passage from formal indicial umbral calculus to Mellin--Barnes umbral transmutation theory. [...] While the formal procedure reproduces the correct results in suitable convergence chambers, it may lead to non-admissible hypergeometric expansions at physically relevant parameter values. The cubic moment provides the basic example [...] We show that this obstruction is removed by replacing the purely formal expansion with an analytic umbral transmutation. In this setting, exponential umbral pairings are interpreted through Mellin--Barnes integrals, and Ramanujan's Master Theorem acts as an inverse selection principle for the spectral ground state, or clock, associated with a given Bessel product. The factorisation \(J_0^3=J_0J_0^2\) produces two distinct clocks and reduces the cubic full-line moment to a one-dimensional Barnes integral, equivalently to a Meijer \(G\)-function. This gives the classical value of the cubic Bessel moment and clarifies why the divergent Appell realisation is only a local representation of a globally meaningful umbral identity. The same mechanism is then applied to scaled cubic products and to the fourth Bessel moment. [...] The fifth moment marks the first genuinely higher-rank case: the natural umbral grouping leads to a bivariate Barnes transmutation rather than to an ordinary Meijer \(G\)-function. Finally, we discuss real fractional powers \(J_0^\alpha\), \(\alpha>2\), showing that the same interpretation persists beyond integer moments. [...] The resulting picture identifies Bessel moments as values of effective umbral transmutations and separates the global analytic meaning of the umbral representation from the local convergence properties of its hypergeometric residue expansions.
tldr: The paper develops an analytic umbral approach to compute Bessel moments, using Mellin-Barnes integrals and Ramanujan's Master Theorem to resolve divergences in hypergeometric expansions.
motivation: To provide a rigorous analytic framework for Bessel moments, which arise in physics but suffer from divergent formal expansions at physically relevant parameters.
method: The authors replace formal umbral calculus with analytic umbral transmutation, interpreting exponential pairings via Mellin-Barnes integrals and using Ramanujan's Master Theorem as an inverse selection principle.
result: They show that the cubic Bessel moment reduces to a Meijer G-function, resolving the divergence of the Appell realization, and extend the method to higher moments and fractional powers.
conclusion: Bessel moments are identified as values of effective umbral transmutations, separating global analytic meaning from local convergence properties of hypergeometric expansions.

title: A Comprehensive Survey On Semantic Communication In Non-Terrestrial Networks: Architectures, Methodologies, And Challenges
authors: Loc X. Nguyen, Avi Deb Raha, Huy Q. Le, Zhu Han, Eui-Nam Huh, Choong Seon Hong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The sixth-generation wireless networks are envisioned to deliver ubiquitous, seamless, and intelligent connectivity that reaches far beyond the limits of terrestrial infrastructure. Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) are central to this vision, extending coverage to underserved regions, remote terrain, and disaster zones that terrestrial deployment cannot economically reach. However, NTN architecture faces numerous limitations: severe path loss over long distances, long propagation delays, large and time-varying Doppler shifts, limited visibility windows, and tight on-board energy and computing budgets. Semantic communication (SemCom), which conveys the meaning of data rather than its raw bit-level representation, is unusually well matched to these conditions: extreme compression rate for task-oriented eases bandwidth scarcity, deep joint source-channel coding prevents the cliff effect due to low signal-to-noise ratio, and generative-AI reconstructs content from sparse cues that survive rain-faded or blocked links. This observation, that each NTN limitation maps onto a SemCom property that addresses it, motivates our survey. We first walk through the NTN limitations one by one, pairing each with the SemCom design choices that complement it, then we organize the literature along three axes: the NTN platform, the semantic methodology, and the supporting techniques, and follow this with platform-by-platform deep dives on satellite-centric, UAV/HAPS-centric, and integrated SAGIN systems. The survey concludes by identifying open research problems, gaps in existing standards, and future directions, including the application of foundation models, energy-aware scheduling, and quantum-assisted SemCom for deep space communication.
tldr: A survey on semantic communication in non-terrestrial networks, mapping NTN limitations to SemCom advantages.
motivation: NTNs face severe path loss, delays, Doppler shifts, and energy constraints; SemCom offers extreme compression and robust joint source-channel coding.
method: The paper organizes literature by NTN platform, semantic methodology, and supporting techniques, with deep dives on satellite, UAV/HAPS, and SAGIN systems.
result: Each NTN limitation is paired with a SemCom property that addresses it; the survey identifies open problems and future directions.
conclusion: SemCom is promising for NTNs, but challenges remain in standardization, energy-aware scheduling, and quantum-assisted SemCom for deep space.

title: Bounded Deep Unfolding For Joint Beamforming And Scheduling In Multi-Cell Mimo Networks
authors: Jiansheng Li, Shuqi Chai, Fan Xu, Kaiming Shen, Guangxu Zhu, Junting Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the joint resource block group (RBG) scheduling and beamforming optimization problem for weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization in multi-cell multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) downlink networks. While the Fast Fractional Programming (FastFP) framework provides a reliable model-driven solution, it suffers from conservative continuous beamforming updates and prohibitive computational overhead during the discrete RBG matching phase. To address these bottlenecks, we propose a joint deep unfolding framework comprising two core modules: P-Net and K-Net. For continuous beamforming, P-Net learns an adaptive relaxation factor along the analytical FastFP update direction. By strictly constraining this factor within an ascent-preserving interval, P-Net accelerates the optimization trajectory while rigorously retaining monotonic improvement and stationary-point convergence guarantees. For discrete RBG scheduling, K-Net learns a long-horizon priority policy that guides a low-complexity greedy assignment, effectively preserving the assignment quality while bypassing the high complexity of Hungarian matching. Both networks leverage analytical algorithmic priors and utilize recurrent parameter sharing, enabling flexible inference beyond the training horizon. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed joint framework achieves higher WSR and faster execution times than conventional model-driven baselines, while generalizing robustly across unseen network scales, antenna configurations, and channel conditions without retraining.
tldr: This paper proposes a deep unfolding framework for joint beamforming and scheduling in multi-cell MIMO networks to maximize weighted sum-rate.
motivation: Existing model-driven methods like FastFP suffer from slow convergence and high computational cost in discrete scheduling, motivating a learning-based acceleration.
method: The framework uses two neural modules: P-Net learns an adaptive relaxation factor for beamforming updates with ascent-preserving guarantees, and K-Net learns a priority policy for greedy scheduling, both leveraging algorithmic priors and recurrent parameter sharing.
result: The proposed method achieves higher weighted sum-rate and faster execution than conventional baselines, and generalizes to unseen network scales and configurations without retraining.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that deep unfolding can effectively accelerate optimization while preserving convergence guarantees, with potential for broader application in wireless resource allocation.

title: Gradient Descent At The Edge Of Stability: Free Energy Model And Kinetic Description Of The Two-layer Network
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dynamics of gradient descent in the Edge of Stability regime, where the learning rate is large enough to induce persistent oscillations in the loss and the sharpness. We propose a continuous-time effective model that tracks the evolution of the average trajectory coupled with the time-averaged covariance of its fast oscillations. Our analysis reveals that the natural quantity to monitor in such unstable regimes is an effective free energy, which combines the original risk functional with a curvature-related "entropic" term. Our model allows us to track the envelope of the oscillations even in situations where its dynamics evolve on similar timescales as the averaged weights. Otherwise stated, we can track the spikes that occur during the training of some neural network architectures. For wide two-layer neural networks optimized under stable non-vanishing oscillations, we derive a mean-field limit that results in a novel kinetic equation describing the joint distribution of weights and their fluctuations. We show that this equation can be interpreted as a Wasserstein-2 gradient flow of a macroscopic free energy. Finally, we provide numerical evidence on matrix factorization and deep learning tasks (CIFAR-10) to demonstrate the model's accuracy in capturing the envelope of the oscillations and the predictive power of the effective free energy.
tldr: This paper studies gradient descent dynamics in the Edge of Stability regime for two-layer neural networks, proposing a free energy model and kinetic description.
motivation: To understand the persistent oscillations in loss and sharpness observed when training neural networks with large learning rates.
method: Develops a continuous-time effective model coupling average trajectory with time-averaged covariance of fast oscillations, and derives a mean-field limit leading to a kinetic equation.
result: Identifies an effective free energy combining risk with curvature-related entropy, enabling tracking of oscillation envelopes; validated on matrix factorization and CIFAR-10.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical framework for training dynamics at the edge of stability, with potential implications for understanding generalization in deep learning.

title: The Complex Spectral Flow: Spectral Conditions For Two-Parameter Equivariant Bifurcation Guarantees

motivation: To simplify the computation of bifurcation invariants in symmetric systems by bypassing traditional degree factorization and Burnside ring multiplication.

conclusion: Provides a spectral approach to bifurcation analysis that may simplify proofs and enable new applications in equivariant dynamical systems.

title: A Two-Channel F-Transform Representation For Early Trajectory Characterization In Iterated Correlation Dynamics
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many nonlinear iterative procedures generate high-dimensional trajectories whose early behavior is informative but difficult to compare directly. This paper studies a soft-computing representation problem: how to convert a short early trajectory segment into compact, interpretable, fixed-dimensional fuzzy coordinates that preserve information about subsequent convergence and trajectory geometry. The problem is investigated for iterated Pearson correlation matrices, a nonlinear matrix iteration historically connected with CONCOR-type blockmodeling and repeated-correlation methods. The proposed descriptor uses two logarithmic signals from the early post-transient regime: a step-size signal, measuring contraction magnitude, and a contraction-ratio signal, measuring local contraction evolution. Each signal is projected onto a three-node triangular fuzzy partition using zero-degree F-transform coefficients and one centered first-degree coefficient. This yields an eight-dimensional two-channel representation separating local level from local trend and contraction magnitude from contraction evolution. Across 22 matrix dimensions with 1000 trajectories per dimension, the descriptor is compared with raw trajectory samples, statistical summaries, and PCA-compressed raw features using Random Forest regression for convergence-length approximation. It achieves mean R^2 = 0.6480, close to raw trajectories (0.6518) and statistical summaries (0.6528), while improving over the step-size-only F-transform descriptor (0.5001). Repeated random-split and shifted-window experiments confirm stability. PCA and clustering further show reproducible low-dimensional organization, with the first two principal components explaining 84.26% of variance and k = 3 favored by the mean silhouette criterion.
tldr: This paper proposes a fuzzy representation method for early trajectory characterization in iterated correlation dynamics, using F-transform coefficients to compress short trajectory segments into interpretable features.
motivation: To convert short early trajectory segments from nonlinear iterative procedures into compact, interpretable, fixed-dimensional fuzzy coordinates that preserve information about subsequent convergence and trajectory geometry.
method: Two logarithmic signals (step-size and contraction-ratio) from early post-transient regime are projected onto triangular fuzzy partitions using zero-degree and first-degree F-transform coefficients, yielding an eight-dimensional two-channel representation. Random Forest regression is used for convergence-length approximation.
result: The descriptor achieves mean R^2 = 0.6480, close to raw trajectories (0.6518) and statistical summaries (0.6528), and improves over step-size-only descriptor (0.5001). PCA shows first two components explain 84.26% variance.
conclusion: The proposed representation is effective for early trajectory characterization in iterated correlation dynamics, with potential applications in soft computing and data analysis, but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Experimental Design For Passive Imaging Source Problems
authors: Christian Aarset, Thorsten Hohage, Georg Stadler
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work focuses on optimal experimental design (OED) methods for passive imaging. We adopt a Bayesian inverse problem framework for passive imaging source problems, primarily focusing on spatially uncorrelated sources and systems governed by the Helmholtz equation. A major challenge in passive imaging is that the use of correlation data causes the observation dimension to grow quadratically with the number of sensor locations, compounding the computational difficulty of finding optimal designs. To overcome the computational bottleneck of repeated PDE solves in optimal design algorithms, we develop a two-level, low-rank approximation of the A-optimal design objective. This effectively decouples the problem into an offline and an online phase, enabling efficient evaluation of the design objective and its gradient without additional PDE solves. Our numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm efficiently scales to large problems and that the resulting optimal designs significantly outperform random sensor placements in minimizing posterior uncertainty.
tldr: This paper develops efficient computational methods for optimal experimental design in passive imaging source problems governed by the Helmholtz equation.
motivation: Passive imaging source problems face computational challenges due to quadratic growth of observation dimension with sensor count, making optimal design computationally expensive.
method: A Bayesian inverse problem framework is adopted, and a two-level low-rank approximation of the A-optimal design objective is developed to decouple the problem into offline and online phases, avoiding repeated PDE solves.
result: The proposed algorithm scales efficiently to large problems, and optimal designs significantly outperform random sensor placements in minimizing posterior uncertainty.
conclusion: The method enables practical optimal experimental design for large-scale passive imaging, with potential extensions to other inverse problems.

title: Robust Repair Of Reed-Solomon Codes
authors: Wilton Kim, Stanislav Kruglik, Gaojun Luo, Han Mao Kiah
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of robust repair of a single erasure in Reed--Solomon codes under low communication bandwidth. Focusing on the Guruswami--Wootters trace repair framework, we investigate whether a failed node can be correctly repaired in the presence of erroneous responses from helper nodes. Equivalently, we view the collection of downloaded traces as a code, which we call the repair-trace code. By characterizing the zero coefficients of the associated polynomial in terms of cyclotomic cosets, we derive upper bounds on the dimension [MATH] that allow correction of a given number of erroneous traces [MATH], as well as lower bounds on the minimum distance as a function of [MATH]. For the case [MATH], we exploit explicit formulas for cyclotomic coset representatives to obtain the exact optimal dimension bound for single-error correction. We also propose two efficient robust repair schemes. Our first scheme achieves the error-correction capability guaranteed by the BCH bound. To approach a stronger bound based on character sums, we develop a second scheme that tolerates more errors at the cost of an additional factor [MATH] in computational complexity.
tldr: This paper studies robust repair of Reed-Solomon codes under erroneous helper responses, focusing on the Guruswami-Wootters trace repair framework.
motivation: To ensure correct repair of a failed node in distributed storage systems even when helper nodes provide erroneous responses, improving reliability.
method: Characterizes zero coefficients of associated polynomials via cyclotomic cosets to derive bounds on repair-trace code dimension and minimum distance; proposes two efficient robust repair schemes.
result: Derives upper bounds on dimension for correcting a given number of errors and lower bounds on minimum distance; obtains exact optimal dimension bound for single-error correction when q=2; first scheme achieves BCH bound, second tolerates more errors with higher complexity.
conclusion: Provides theoretical bounds and practical schemes for robust repair of Reed-Solomon codes, with implications for error-correcting codes in distributed storage.

title: Asymmetry Of Entropy Invariants For Generic Mixing $Z^n$-Actions
authors: Valery V. Ryzhikov Mikhail V. Engelgardt
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose that for a mixing [MATH]-action, [MATH], there exists a Kirillov-Kushnirenko entropy that is zero for this action and completely positive for its inverse. We prove that this property is generic for the mixing [MATH]-actions.

title: Bv Construction Of Susy Vertex Algebras From Susy Factorization Algebras

title: Compositional Boundaries For Density Fusion
authors: Ratan Bahadur Thapa, Ali Darijani, J\"urgen Beyerer, Steffen Staab
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed uncertainty-management systems often combine local probabilistic models along aggregation trees chosen by communication, privacy, or scheduling constraints. The final density should depend on the weighted sources, not on the particular order in which intermediate nodes combine them. We study this requirement as an algebraic compositionality problem for binary fusion of weighted probability densities. The central question is when a local fusion rule can be executed hierarchically while remaining order-invariant. We establish a compositional boundary for local segment-valued fusion rules. Within the class of continuous binary rules with additive output weights and weight-only coefficients, order-invariant hierarchical execution characterizes normalized weighted linear pooling; norm-induced segment balancing realizes the corresponding coefficient. Smooth endpoint-to-candidate [MATH]-divergence balancing has a different local geometry: its quadratic expansion induces square-root effective weights, showing why pairwise solvability alone is insufficient for schedule-independent fusion. We show that this obstruction is local to endpoint-to-candidate binary balancing, whereas global divergence barycenters retain additive-weight local limits. Finally, Gaussian mixtures show how the same issue appears in finite model classes: exact fusion is compositional, whereas stepwise compression is compositional only under a congruence condition on unnormalized component measures. These results distinguish exact schedule-independent fusion from global aggregation objectives and local approximation heuristics.
tldr: This paper studies order-invariant hierarchical fusion of weighted probability densities, establishing that normalized weighted linear pooling is the only continuous binary rule with additive output weights that allows schedule-independent composition.
motivation: Distributed uncertainty-management systems combine local probabilistic models along aggregation trees, but the final density should depend only on weighted sources, not on the order of combination. The paper aims to characterize when local fusion rules can be executed hierarchically while remaining order-invariant.
method: The authors formulate the problem as an algebraic compositionality problem for binary fusion of weighted probability densities. They analyze continuous binary rules with additive output weights and weight-only coefficients, and examine local geometry of divergence balancing.
result: Order-invariant hierarchical execution characterizes normalized weighted linear pooling; norm-induced segment balancing realizes the corresponding coefficient. Smooth endpoint-to-candidate f-divergence balancing has a different local geometry that prevents schedule-independent fusion, whereas global divergence barycenters retain additive-weight local limits.
conclusion: The results distinguish exact schedule-independent fusion from global aggregation objectives and local approximation heuristics, with implications for distributed fusion systems.

title: Direct Reconstruction For Acoustic Inverse Born Scattering
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the inverse medium scattering problem for the Helmholtz equation in two dimensions, i.e., the task to recover a compactly supported penetrable two-dimensional scatterer from full knowledge of the associated far field data or, equivalently, the far field operator. Although this problem is uniquely solvable, it is severely ill-posed and nonlinear. In the regime of weak scattering, the Born approximation yields a linearized relation between the contrast and the far field data, thus overcoming the second difficulty. This linear setting allows to build on recent work on linearized electrical impedance tomography, which relies on triangular Zernike decompositions, to derive an explicit reconstruction formula that expresses the expansion coefficients of the contrast in terms of those of the far field data. By choosing the expansion functions appropriately, the resulting system matrix decouples into separate (infinite) triangular systems for the spatial angular frequencies in the contrast. Consequently, each of these systems can be solved independently by performing forward substitutions. Our numerical experiments indicate that this approach, combined with an adequate regularization method, remains effective even when applied to full nonlinear far field data beyond the Born regime.
tldr: This paper presents a direct reconstruction method for the acoustic inverse Born scattering problem using triangular Zernike decompositions.
motivation: To overcome the nonlinearity and ill-posedness of the inverse medium scattering problem for the Helmholtz equation by leveraging the Born approximation and developing an explicit reconstruction formula.
method: The authors use triangular Zernike decompositions to linearize the problem under the Born approximation, resulting in a decoupled triangular system for the expansion coefficients of the contrast, which can be solved via forward substitution.
result: Numerical experiments show that the method remains effective even when applied to full nonlinear far field data beyond the Born regime, with appropriate regularization.
conclusion: The approach provides a fast, direct reconstruction algorithm for acoustic inverse scattering, with potential extensions to other wave-based imaging modalities.

title: Willing But Unable: Separating Refusal From Capability In Code LLMs Via Abliteration
authors: Cristina Carleo, Pietro Liguori, Naghmeh Ivaki, Domenico Cotroneo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Producing a labeled vulnerable code at scale is a recurring obstacle for learning-based vulnerability detection: mined corpora carry substantial label noise, and existing LLM-based augmentation propagates these inaccuracies because it transforms vulnerable seeds rather than synthesising vulnerabilities from a specification. A complementary route is to start from safe code and ask an instruction-tuned LLM to inject a specified CWE (which would shift the labeling burden from open-ended detection to bounded binary confirmation) but safety-aligned code LLMs systematically refuse such prompts. This paper is a preliminary feasibility study of abliteration, a low-rank weight edit that orthogonally projects out the refusal direction in the residual stream, as a tool to remove this barrier. We use Python and CWE-89 (SQL injection) as a case study, evaluating the Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct family at 3B, 7B, and 14B parameters on safe samples drawn from PromSec and SafeCoder, replicated three times per condition. We find that (i) refusal on injection prompts is strongly size- and prompt-context-dependent: the 14B refuses 100% of prompts, the 7B refuses 73% of PromSec but only 5% of SafeCoder, whereas the 3B is essentially never blocked; (ii) abliteration reduces refusal to zero or near-zero across all sizes while leaving syntactic validity above 93%, supporting the view that, in this setting, refusal can be detached from measured code-generation capability; and (iii) the post-abliteration injection rate remains capacity-bound (88-97% on the 14B, 89-90% on the 7B, and 25-48% on the 3B) separating willingness, which abliteration unlocks, from capability, which scales with parameters. Vulnerability verdicts are produced by a three-tool detector ensemble (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit) followed by manual adjudication by two authors on detector-positive outputs.
tldr: This paper explores abliteration, a weight-editing technique to bypass safety alignment in code LLMs, enabling them to inject vulnerabilities into safe code for generating labeled datasets.
motivation: To address the lack of large-scale labeled vulnerable code for training vulnerability detectors, the authors investigate whether safety-aligned code LLMs can be made to inject specific vulnerabilities (CWE-89) via a low-rank weight edit called abliteration.
method: The study applies abliteration to Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct models (3B, 7B, 14B) by projecting out the refusal direction in the residual stream, then prompts them to inject SQL injection into safe code samples from PromSec and SafeCoder. Vulnerability detection is performed by a three-tool ensemble (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit) with manual adjudication.
result: Abliteration reduces refusal to near-zero across all model sizes while maintaining syntactic validity above 93%. Injection rates are capacity-bound: 88-97% for 14B, 89-90% for 7B, and 25-48% for 3B, showing that willingness (refusal) can be separated from capability.
conclusion: Abliteration effectively removes refusal behavior in code LLMs for vulnerability injection, enabling scalable dataset generation, but the approach raises ethical concerns about misuse and requires careful consideration of safety implications.

title: Rh+: Row-Hit-Optimized Scheduling For PIM-based Llm Inference
authors: Yongchan Jung, Shafayat Mowla Anik, Byeong Kil Lee, Jeeho Ryoo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model inference on processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures promises to break the memory wall by performing multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations directly within HBM3 DRAM banks. Prior work identifies the power constraint timing parameter nCCDAB as the primary performance bottleneck and optimizes scheduling accordingly. We demonstrate that for GEMV operations that dominate autoregressive decoding, the DRAM row cycle time (nRC) is 10 to 11 times larger than nCCDAB. Consequently, nCCDAB is entirely masked, rendering prior nCCDAB-focused optimizations ineffective for these workloads. The root cause is inherited host-centric address interleaving, which forces every all-bank MAC command into a different DRAM row. We propose RH+ scheduling, a simple stride change that keeps 32 consecutive MAC operations within the same row. Cycle-accurate simulation across four LLM workloads shows that RH+ delivers 8-12x speedup, over 74% energy reduction, and up to 52x EDP improvement.
tldr: This paper proposes a row-hit-optimized scheduling technique for PIM-based LLM inference to improve performance and energy efficiency.
motivation: Prior PIM scheduling optimizations focused on the nCCDAB timing parameter, but for GEMV operations in LLM inference, the row cycle time nRC is the dominant bottleneck, making previous optimizations ineffective.
method: The authors identify that host-centric address interleaving causes frequent row misses, and propose RH+ scheduling, a simple stride change that keeps 32 consecutive MAC operations within the same DRAM row.
result: Cycle-accurate simulation across four LLM workloads shows 8-12x speedup, over 74% energy reduction, and up to 52x EDP improvement.
conclusion: RH+ effectively addresses the row-cycle bottleneck in PIM-based LLM inference, offering significant performance and energy gains with minimal hardware changes.

title: Wave Focusing In Metamaterials: Tactile Displays Beyond The Diffraction Limit
authors: Gregory Reardon, Max Linnander, Dustin Goetz, Neeli Tummala, Yon Visell
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the challenge of engineering distributed haptic displays capable of reproducing multiple localized, independently addressable vibrations -- representing virtual tactile pixels -- at arbitrary locations on a surface. Our technique is based on the focusing of mechanical waves in a flexural plate using a sparse set of actuators. At tactile frequencies, wave diffraction prevents the formation of localized virtual tactile pixels at spatial scales relevant for multi-digit touch interactions. We overcome this limitation by augmenting the plate with a lattice of mechanical resonators, forming a locally resonant metamaterial plate. Coupling between the plate's dynamic modes and those of the resonators alters the dispersion relation governing wave transmission, introducing a slow-wave branch that enables focusing beyond the diffraction limit imposed by the unmodified plate. We use numerical simulations to engineer the dispersion relation of the metamaterial system for high-resolution focusing at tactile frequencies. We then fabricate a metamaterial tactile display and experimentally demonstrate virtual pixels that are far more localized than those generated on an otherwise identical plate without resonators, resulting in a tenfold reduction in virtual-pixel area. In behavioral experiments, we show that this system can deliver perceptually localized single- and multi-point tactile feedback and moving tactile sources while maintaining independent control over temporal waveforms at multiple display locations. The methods reported here can enable high-resolution haptic displays for widespread applications using a small number of actuated degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper uses metamaterial wave focusing to create high-resolution tactile displays, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To overcome diffraction limits in haptic displays for multi-touch interactions.
method: A locally resonant metamaterial plate alters the dispersion relation to enable subwavelength focusing of mechanical waves.
result: Tenfold reduction in virtual-pixel area and perceptually localized tactile feedback demonstrated.
conclusion: Enables high-resolution haptic displays with few actuators, applicable to virtual reality and human-machine interfaces.

title: TinyML-Driven Cybersecurity For Autonomous Spacecraft: Latency-Accuracy Analysis For Sparta Rf And Cyber Threat Detection
authors: van Le, Trevor Tran, Tan Le
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous spacecraft require rapid, lightweight, and reliable onboard detection of cyber-RF threats. Using the SPARTA attack model, we analyze the latency-accuracy trade-offs of TinyML-compatible classical models -- Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP -- for detecting uplink jamming, Fake-NR spoofing, payload manipulation, ground-segment compromise, and unauthorized command injection. We present a physics-informed theoretical analysis of each model's computational complexity, VC dimension, Lipschitz continuity, and latency scaling, supported by empirical measurements on adversarial RF spectrograms generated via BandErasure, FakeNR, and NoiseBurst corruption modes. Results show that Logistic Regression achieves microsecond-level inference with only a 1\% accuracy drop relative to Random Forest, making it an effective TinyML baseline for onboard autonomy. The study also identifies opportunities for advancing spacecraft cybersecurity through richer feature encoders and multi-timescale learning architectures, building on recent progress in edge intelligence and trustworthy AI.
tldr: This paper evaluates TinyML models for cyber-RF threat detection in autonomous spacecraft, focusing on latency-accuracy trade-offs.
motivation: Autonomous spacecraft need lightweight, real-time onboard detection of cyber-RF threats, but existing solutions may be too slow or heavy.
method: The authors analyze Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP using the SPARTA attack model, with physics-informed complexity analysis and empirical tests on adversarial RF spectrograms.
result: Logistic Regression achieves microsecond inference with only 1% accuracy drop compared to Random Forest, making it a suitable TinyML baseline.
conclusion: The study suggests future work on richer feature encoders and multi-timescale learning for improved spacecraft cybersecurity.

title: Exploring Cooperation Mechanisms Via Reinforcement Learning In Network Common-pool Resource Games
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustaining cooperation in resource-constrained populations requires allocation mechanisms that balance individual incentives, resource sustainability, and distributional fairness. This paper proposes a network common-pool resource game in which individuals are embedded in complex networks, participate in multiple overlapping local resource pools, and face endogenous resource constraints during strategy evolution. Within this framework, we first examine two representative allocation mechanisms, equal allocation and proportional allocation. The results show that equal allocation produces fair but inefficient outcomes by weakening contribution incentives, whereas proportional allocation can temporarily promote cooperation but amplifies accumulated advantages and leads to severe inequality. To overcome these limitations, we develop a graph neural network-based reinforcement learning framework in which a learned social planner allocates local pool resources without directly controlling individual strategies. Simulation results under four representative network topologies show that the learned planner sustains higher cooperation levels and average accumulated resources, and reduces inequality compared with the baselines. Furthermore, we interpret the learned policy and distill it into two simpler mechanisms: a resource-dependent mixture mechanism for regular networks and a degree-conditioned mixture mechanism for heterogeneous networks. These mechanisms reveal that effective allocation should adapt to both local resource states and structural positions, providing an interpretable route from reinforcement learning policy search to mechanism design in networked resource-sharing systems.
tldr: This paper uses reinforcement learning to design allocation mechanisms in network common-pool resource games, focusing on cooperation and fairness.
motivation: To overcome limitations of equal and proportional allocation mechanisms in sustaining cooperation and reducing inequality in networked resource-sharing systems.
method: Proposes a graph neural network-based reinforcement learning framework where a learned social planner allocates local pool resources without directly controlling individual strategies.
result: The learned planner sustains higher cooperation levels, average accumulated resources, and reduces inequality compared to baselines; the policy is distilled into simpler mechanisms for regular and heterogeneous networks.
conclusion: Effective allocation should adapt to local resource states and structural positions, providing an interpretable route from RL policy search to mechanism design.

title: Scaling Matters Of Cell Fate
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports a universal scaling law in DNA methylation dynamics during early embryo development, suggesting physical constraints govern cell fate.
motivation: To understand whether cell differentiation is driven by molecular specifics or universal physical principles.
method: Analysis of methylation dynamics in early embryos, likely using high-throughput sequencing and scaling analysis.
result: Methylation dynamics follow a universal scaling law, independent of molecular details.
conclusion: Physical constraints may shape cell fate, implying a fundamental principle in developmental biology.

title: Decoupling Adhesion From Jamming In Phase Transitions Drives Tissue Organization
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how adhesion and jamming phase transitions drive tissue organization in cellular collectives, using in silico and in vivo experiments.
motivation: To understand how multiple control parameters, specifically cell density and adhesion, influence phase transitions and material states in tissues, and how these transitions direct developmental programs.
method: The authors independently tuned cell density and adhesion in both computational models (in silico) and living organisms (in vivo) to observe their effects on tissue material state and organization.
result: Adhesion dictates the tissue material state; adhesion-driven solidification in unjammed pluripotent tissues drives epithelial organization, revealing that phase transitions direct developmental programmes.
conclusion: The findings uncover a mechanism where adhesion controls tissue material properties and organization, with implications for developmental biology and tissue engineering.

title: Thorium-229 Lifetime Locked Down
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 May 2026;
tldr: The paper resolves a decade-long puzzle about the anomalously short lifetime of a nuclear metastable state in thorium-229 ions, revealing an uncommon decay channel.
motivation: The lifetime of the nuclear metastable state in singly charged thorium-229 ions appeared shorter than theoretical predictions, puzzling physicists for about ten years.
method: The study likely involved experimental measurements of the decay rate and theoretical modeling to identify the decay channel.
result: The solution provides evidence for an uncommon decay channel that explains the observed shorter lifetime.
conclusion: The findings resolve a long-standing discrepancy and may have implications for nuclear clocks and fundamental physics.

title: X-Band UAV-enabled Integrated Sensing And Communications For Vehicular Networks
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly considered as aerial platforms capable of providing both sensing and communication services, representing a promising paradigm for intelligent transportation systems. This paper investigates the optimal time allocation for a UAV-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISaC) system operating in the X-band for vehicular networks. We analyze the trade-off between sensing accuracy and communication performance under practical UAV constraints and fading effects, considering both single-shadowing and double-shadowing channel models. An optimization framework is developed to allocate time between sensing and communication while guaranteeing minimum communication rates and sufficient sensing reliability. Simulation results demonstrate adaptive time allocation strategies, highlighting how UAV-to-ground channel conditions and target distances influence the balance between sensing and communication in smart mobility scenarios.
tldr: This paper studies time allocation for UAV-based integrated sensing and communication in vehicular networks, focusing on X-band performance trade-offs.
motivation: To optimize the dual use of UAVs for sensing and communication in intelligent transportation systems, addressing practical constraints like fading and shadowing.
method: An optimization framework is developed to allocate time between sensing and communication, considering single- and double-shadowing channel models and UAV constraints.
result: Adaptive time allocation strategies are demonstrated, showing how channel conditions and target distances affect the sensing-communication balance.
conclusion: The work provides insights for deploying UAV-enabled ISaC in smart mobility, but is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: The Ize Conjecture Redux: A Parity Criterion For Global Equivariant Bifurcation Guarantees
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Ize Conjecture proposed that every absolutely irreducible representation of a compact Lie group admits a maximal isotropy subgroup with an odd-dimensional fixed-point space, which would provide a universal bifurcation guarantee via the equivariant degree. Its disproof by Lauterbach and Matthews necessitates a more targeted criterion. We introduce Ize pairs -- pairs [MATH] for which some maximal isotropy subgroup [MATH] satisfies [MATH] -- and prove that this dimension-parity condition completely captures the algebraic obstruction to a non-trivial equivariant degree change at maximal orbit types. Integrating this criterion with a mod-2 equivariant spectral flow yields local and global bifurcation guarantees without recourse to Burnside ring arithmetic. As an application, we establish unbounded branches of non-stationary periodic solutions in a [MATH]-symmetric coupled oscillator network, where the bifurcation guarantees follow entirely from the crossing parity of the linearization at the boundary of a regular parameter window.
tldr: The paper introduces a parity criterion for global equivariant bifurcation guarantees in dynamical systems, unrelated to quantum information or condensed matter physics.
motivation: To provide a more targeted criterion for global bifurcation guarantees after the disproof of the Ize Conjecture.
method: Introduces Ize pairs and a mod-2 equivariant spectral flow to capture algebraic obstructions to nontrivial equivariant degree change.
result: The dimension-parity condition completely captures the obstruction, yielding local and global bifurcation guarantees without Burnside ring arithmetic.
conclusion: The criterion is applied to a coupled oscillator network, establishing unbounded branches of periodic solutions.

title: On Strong Identities Of Almost-canonically Seminormed Rings
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the strong identity condition (SIC) for almost-canonically seminormed rings, a class of topological graded rings that includes enveloping algebras of vertex operator algebras. This condition was introduced in the algebro-geometric theory of conformal blocks, where it governs the smoothing of nodal curves. To understand the representation-theoretic meaning of SIC, we develop the representation theory of almost-canonically seminormed rings, including Zhu-type algebras, induced modules, rationality conditions, tensor product compatibility, and an end formula for the mode transition algebra. Our main result characterizes the strong identity condition in terms of orthogonal expansions, projectivity of canonical modules, and Morita-type equivalences induced by Zhu-type algebras. As an application, we show that for vertex operator algebras of CFT type, the smoothing property is equivalent to the Zhu algebra inducing a Morita-type equivalence with the category of admissible modules. Consequently, the strong identity condition identifies the precise representation-theoretic obstruction to extending algebraic smoothing beyond the semisimple setting. We further illustrate the theory through explicit examples, including the Weyl algebra and several irrational vertex operator algebras where the strong identity condition fails.
tldr: This paper studies strong identity conditions for almost-canonically seminormed rings in the context of vertex operator algebras and conformal blocks, with no connection to the user's research interests.
motivation: To understand the representation-theoretic meaning of the strong identity condition (SIC) introduced in the algebro-geometric theory of conformal blocks, which governs smoothing of nodal curves.
method: Develops representation theory of almost-canonically seminormed rings, including Zhu-type algebras, induced modules, rationality conditions, tensor product compatibility, and an end formula for the mode transition algebra.
result: Characterizes SIC in terms of orthogonal expansions, projectivity of canonical modules, and Morita-type equivalences induced by Zhu-type algebras. Shows that for vertex operator algebras of CFT type, smoothing property is equivalent to Zhu algebra inducing a Morita-type equivalence with admissible modules.
conclusion: SIC identifies the precise representation-theoretic obstruction to extending algebraic smoothing beyond the semisimple setting, illustrated by examples where SIC fails.

title: Dimensionality Reduction For Cyberattack Classification: A Comparative Evaluation Of Pca And Linear Predictive Coding
authors: Nelly Elsayed, Zag Elsayed, Navid Asadizanjani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional feature representations are widely used in machine learning-based cyberattack detection systems. However, they increase computational complexity and may hinder deployment in resource-constrained environments. In this paper, we investigate feature compression techniques for cyberattack classification by comparing two dimensionality reduction approaches: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Linear Predictive Coding (LPC). Compressed feature representations with varying dimensionalities are generated and evaluated across several classification models. Experimental analysis demonstrates that PCA preserves classification performance even under aggressive compression. On the other hand, LPC provides competitive predictive representations with slightly larger performance degradation. The results show that substantial reductions in feature dimensionality can be achieved with minimal impact on classification accuracy, highlighting the potential of lightweight feature compression for efficient cybersecurity analytics.
